records.summary: Alphabet guides FY2026 CapEx to $175-185 billion, with investments ramping through the year.
records.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

evidence.quote: our 2026 CapEx investments are anticipated to be in the range of $175 billion to $185 billion

records.summary: CFO reiterates FY2026 CapEx guidance of $175-185 billion, ramping over the year.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

evidence.quote: For the full year 2026, we expect CapEx to be in the range of $175 billion to $185 billion, with investments ramping over the course of the year.

qualifiers.quote: Keep in mind that the availability of supply, pricing of components, and timing of cash payments can cause some variability in the reported CapEx number.

records.summary: AI investments and infrastructure are driving revenue and growth; CapEx aims to meet customer demand and capture opportunities.
records.speaker: Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet and Google

evidence.quote: Overall, we’re seeing our AI investments and infrastructure drive revenue and growth across the board. To meet customer demand and capitalize on the growing opportunities ahead of us

records.summary: AI investments are translating to strong performance, reinforcing conviction to invest further in the AI opportunity.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

evidence.quote: the investments we have been making in AI are already translating to strong performance across the business, as you've seen in our financial results. Our successful execution, coupled with strong performance, reinforces our conviction to make the investments required to further capitalize on the AI opportunity.

records.summary: CapEx funds AI compute for DeepMind frontier models, Google Services UX and advertiser ROI, Cloud demand, and Other Bets.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

evidence.quote: We're investing in AI compute capacity to support frontier model development by Google DeepMind, ongoing efforts to improve the user experience, and drive higher advertiser ROI in Google Services, significant Cloud customer demand, as well as strategic investments in Other Bets.

records.summary: Significant Cloud demand expected to drive strong growth despite a tight supply environment.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

evidence.quote: In Google Cloud, we're seeing significant demand for our products and services, which we expect to continue to drive strong growth, despite the tight supply environment we're operating in.

records.summary: Higher technical infrastructure investment will pressure the P&L via increased depreciation and data center operating costs such as energy.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

evidence.quote: the significant increase in our investments in technical infrastructure will continue to put pressure on the P&L in the form of higher depreciation expense and related data centers' operations costs such as energy.

records.summary: FY2025 depreciation was $21.1 billion, up nearly $6 billion or 38% from $15.3 billion in 2024.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

evidence.quote: In 2025, depreciation increased by nearly $6 billion, or 38%, from $15.3 billion in 2024, to $21.1 billion in 2025.

records.summary: 2026 depreciation growth is expected to accelerate in Q1 and meaningfully increase for the full year given recent CapEx increases.
records.speaker: Anat Ashkenazi, SVP and CFO, Alphabet and Google

evidence.quote: Given the increase in our CapEx investments in recent years, we expect the growth rate in 2026 depreciation to accelerate in Q1, and meaningfully increase for the full year.
